title: Interlayer interactions reshape charge-density wave through electronic elasticity in 4H$_{\mathrm{b}}$-TaS$_2$
authors: Carolina A. Marques, Martha Rösler, Berk Zengin, Aleš Cahlík, Edoardo Martino, Konstantin Semeniuk, Helmuth Berger, László Forró, Ana Akrap, Fabian D. Natterer
abstract: Incommensurate charge-density waves (CDWs) in layered quantum materials frequently exhibit widely varying ordering wave vectors, even among nominally identical samples, obscuring their intrinsic electronic properties. Here we identify an inherent origin of this variability through the electronic elasticity of an incommensurate CDW using the model heterostructure 4H$_{\mathrm{b}}$-TaS$_2$, composed of alternating commensurate CDW on 1T and incommensurate CDW on 1H layers. Low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy, combined with Fourier and quasiparticle-interference analysis, exploits the lattice-pinned 1T CDW as an internal reference to resolve discrete compressive ($-2.3\%$) and tensile ($+3.2\%$) elastic states of the neighboring 1H CDW selected by the interlayer registry of the adjacent layers. Corresponding few-meV shifts of a flat band demonstrate that weak interlayer interactions reshape the low-energy electronic structure through the intrinsic elasticity of the incommensurate CDW. These findings establish electronic elasticity as a mechanism by which subtle interlayer interactions control correlated electronic states in van der Waals heterostructures.
summary: This work investigates how interlayer forces control the electronic state of Charge-Density Waves (CDWs) in $4	ext{H}_{\mathrm{b}}	ext{-TaS}_2$. By using STM, the authors demonstrated that the CDW wave vector elastically responds to the stacking registry between adjacent layers. This establishes electronic elasticity as a general mechanism by which weak interlayer interactions dictate correlated electronic properties in van der Waals heterostructures.
main_problem: The intrinsic variability of incommensurate Charge-Density Wave (CDW) wave vectors in layered quantum materials obscures their fundamental electronic properties.
main_result: Weak interlayer interactions can reshape the low-energy electronic structure by controlling the CDW ordering wave vector through the inherent electronic elasticity of the CDW state.
method: Low-temperature Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) combined with Fourier and quasiparticle-interference analysis was used to probe distinct elastic states in a model heterostructure.
model_or_system: The study uses the $4	ext{H}_{\mathrm{b}}	ext{-TaS}_2$ heterostructure, modeling alternating commensurate CDWs on 1T layers and incommensurate CDWs on 1H layers to investigate interlayer coupling effects.
key_observables: CDW ordering wave vectors ($\mathbf{q}$), shifts in unoccupied flat bands (few-meV shifts), and moiré patterns observed via STM/FT analysis.
important_parameters: Compressive ($\approx -2.3\%$) and tensile ($\approx +3.2\%$) elastic strain states induced by interlayer registry.
main_assumptions: The CDW wave vector is treated as an intrinsic elastic degree of freedom responsive to external/interlayer strain fields.
figures_summary: Figures show STM images, Fourier transforms revealing distinct CDW peaks based on termination (D1 vs D2), and QPI maps demonstrating energy shifts corresponding to different strain states.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares CDW patterns across different stacking registries (1H-term vs 1T-terminated regions) using STM/FT, linking the observed structural variations to measurable electronic structure changes via flat band shifts.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the concept of an order parameter's elasticity being controlled by weak coupling is analogous to how external fields or interactions can tune quantum phases in superconducting or correlated systems relevant to AMO research.
